behavior_flags.A_emotional_risk_cluster: Pattern of agitation, rigidity, defensiveness, clipped tone
behavior_flags.B_child_contempt_cluster: Sarcasm, contempt, irritation toward children, dismissive labeling
behavior_flags.C_coachability_risk_cluster: Blame pattern, dismissing feedback, dominance, interruptions
behavior_flags.E_zoom_violation: Working during interview, supervising children, calls or multitasking

prompt.content_quote: I always validate feelings. Children just need connection. I name emotions and help them regulate.
observations: Smirks while quoting a child crying
Faster and sharper speech when describing child behavior

required_probe: What did you think the child was feeling in that moment, and what did you feel toward them?

cases.title: Great answers, supervising kids on Zoom

prompt.content_quote: I’m very calm under stress. I slow down, breathe, and keep my voice steady. I’m gentle during routines and always watch cues.
observations: Says 'I’m at work right now but it’s fine'

required_probe: Just to confirm, are you currently working or supervising children right now?

cases.title: Regulation story is good, but dysregulated in interview

prompt.content_quote: When I’m overwhelmed I pause, lower my voice, and focus on steady breathing. Kids co-regulate with us.
observations: Visibly tense when asked about stress
Defensive: 'Why are you asking me that?'

required_probe: Right now, what’s happening for you as we talk about stress?

cases.title: Average answer, exceptional warmth and attunement

prompt.content_quote: I try to be patient and help kids calm down.
observations: Face softens when speaking about a child
Uses child-respect language unprompted: 'They’re having a hard time'

required_probe: Can you walk me through what you noticed in the child, and what you did step by step?

prompt.content_quote: I’m open to feedback and always willing to learn.
observations: When asked for an example: 'My director targeted me. I did nothing wrong. They just didn’t like me.'

required_probe: With hindsight, what would you do differently now?

cases.title: Never happened to me across multiple traits

prompt.content_quote: Kids never really get that upset with me. I don’t get overwhelmed. I can’t think of a time I messed up.

required_probe: Even small examples count. What’s the closest situation you can remember?
When you do feel pressure, what helps you reset?

prompt.content_quote: I love teamwork and communication. I always collaborate.
observations: Dismisses coworker in story: 'They were wrong, so I handled it.'

required_probe: What did you do to understand their perspective before deciding they were wrong?

prompt.content_quote: I use positive guidance. I validate feelings. Sometimes you have to embarrass them a little so they stop.
observations: Uses shaming as an accepted tool

required_probe: What do you mean by 'embarrass' and what do you hope it teaches the child?

prompt.content_quote: I’m careful with babies. I just grab them quick and get it done. They cry either way.

required_probe: What cues tell you to slow down, and what do you do when a baby resists a routine?

cases.title: High scores, one negative cue moment only

prompt.content_quote: Solid examples across traits. On feedback: 'At first I felt defensive, then I asked for specifics and adjusted.'
observations: One brief defensive moment, then recovers quickly

required_probe: What helped you shift from defensiveness to curiosity in that moment?
